newsitem.title: UK: CE Heath to help cash-strapped MGM fund movies.
newsitem.headline: CE Heath to help cash-strapped MGM fund movies.

text.p: London insurance broker CE Heath is in talks with movie giant MGM to provide an insurance guarantee for funding on future productions such as the forthcoming political thriller Red Corner, starring Richard Gere.
The broker has been approached to help guarantee production funding for at least one and perhaps four new films, including the $48 million Red Corner due to start filming in mid-march.
A spokesman for CE Heath confirmed on Thursday that talks were in progress but said he was unable to comment due to confidentiality agreements.

However film insurance experts said the most likely arrangement would be a completion bond, which the studio buys to insure itself against running out of money before a film is finished, therefore reassuring other investors in the project that it will reach the box-office.
The only other movie currently on the studio's production schedule is the new James Bond movie starring Pierce Brosnan, nicknamed "Bond 18', due to start shooting in April for release next Christmas.
According to the Hollywood newspaper Variety, MGM has been under mounting pressure to kick-start its feature film activities.

The company will be operating for the next 12 to 18 months without any substantial revenue to its film division, the main part of the studio's operation. In addition, the company faces annual overheads estimated at around $150 million a year.
In October the studio secured a $350 million credit line from investment bank J.P.Morgan, which MGM chairman Frank Mancuso insists is sufficient to maintain cash flow for production plans.
But Hollywood sources say an atmosphere of concern has grown in the company since it was bought by Kirk Kerkorian and Seven Network for $1.2 billion last Autumn.

The blow dealt by the departure of MGM's top financial adviser Mike Hope has been followed by poorer-than-expected box office returns on recent films such as Fledwas and the Bill Murray comedy Larger than Life.
And recently shooting of the new James Bond movie, on which MGM is banking heavily, was postponed after star Brosnan was injured filming Dante's Peak.
Banking analysts at the time of the MGM sale predicted the studio would need to find new ways of raising cash in the next year or two in order to keep new productions rolling.
